'''Nancy May Gordon''' is an American economist and statistician who works for the [[United States Census Bureau]].

==Education and career==
Gordon majored in economics and statistics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], and earned a doctorate in economics from [[Stanford University]].{{r|welcome}} Her dissertation, ''Ex ante and Ex post Substitutability in Economic Growth'', was supervised by [[Kenneth Arrow]].

After completing her Ph.D., she became a faculty member at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] from 1970 to 1974, and then a senior research associate at the [[Urban Institute]].

In 1979, Gordon was an appointee in the [[Presidency of Jimmy Carter|Carter Administration]] as a senior advisor and executive director of the Presidential Task Force on Women. From 1980 to 1995 she worked in the [[Congressional Budget Office]] as a senior economist and assistant director for health and human resources.{{r|sih}}

Since 1995 she has worked at the [[United States Census Bureau]]. From 1995 until 2005 she worked on household surveys as associate director for demographic programs.{{r|sih}}<ref>U.S. Bureau of the Census, Current Population Reports, P60-203, Measuring 50 Years of Economic Change Using the March Current Population Survey, U.S. Government Printing Office, Washington, DC, 1998. https://www2.census.gov/prod2/popscan/p60-203.pdf</ref> she was the associate director for demographic programs. Subsequently, she became associate director for strategic planning and innovation at the Census Bureau prior to her retirement.<ref>{{Cite web |title=JSM 2002 |url=https://ww2.amstat.org/meetings/jsm/2002/onlineprogram/index.cfm?fuseaction=abstract_details&abstractid=300389 |access-date=2024-08-31 |website=ww2.amstat.org}}</ref>

==Service==
Gordon was president of the [[Caucus for Women in Statistics]] in 1985,{{r|cws}}
and chair of the Committee on the Status of Women in the Economics Profession of the [[American Economic Association]] from 1985 to 1987.{{r|welcome}} She has also served on the board of directors of [[WAEPA|Worldwide Assurance for Employees of Public Agencies]], a nonprofit insurance association for federal employees, from 1982 to 1990, including a term as president of the board.{{r|sih|welcome}}

==Recognition==
In September 2000, Gordon was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fasa}}<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2007-07-03 |title=American Heart Association Newly Elected Fellows, Spring 2007 |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1161/circulationaha.107.184674 |journal=Circulation |volume=116 |issue=1 |doi=10.1161/circulationaha.107.184674 |issn=0009-7322}}</ref> She is also an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|isi}}
